title: Sample 17-13: Marked Intentional Spelling Errors

illustrates.quote: Marked Spelling Errors. When print calls attention to errors by means of a font attribute (e.g., underline, italics, color, highlighting, etc.) the designated words are uncontracted, and the remainder of the passage is contracted.

blocks.text: Read this narrative and rewrite the underlined words that have been spelled incorrectly.

items.text: You know that new person in our <u>sceince</u> class? My <u>nieghbor</u> says he's the <u>hier</u> to a huge fortune!
The <u>hier</u> to a huge fortune going to public school? That's hard to <u>beleive</u>. In fact, it's pretty <u>inconcievable</u>.

print.notes: Directions, then two 'Student' passages, each with several underlined misspelled words mixed into otherwise-contracted text — 17.10.3's own mixed uncontracted/contracted convention.
print.printFeatures: Misspelled words underlined; the rest of each passage in ordinary print.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged (both agreed '17.10.3', matches source). Modeled as three paragraphs; each marked-error word individually backtick-uncontracted inside otherwise-contracted running prose — the same mixed-passage mechanism standards-map.md (BANA 17.10.3) confirms 'done' via probe. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.now: one list, items with marker "Student 1:" / "Student 2:" and the text after the label
printCorrections.evidence: references/_gemini/_done/gold-17-A/page-490.png: the print is a two-item hanging layout - the labels "Student 1:" and "Student 2:" stand at the left margin and the speech text hangs to their right; braille lines 11-18 accordingly start at cell 1 with runover at cell 3 (1-3), not a paragraph indent.

references/_gemini/_done/gold-17-A/page-490.png: the print shows the six misspelled words underlined ("Read this narrative and rewrite the underlined words"); nothing in the print marks them as uncontracted. Braille lines 11-18 show _1 (underline word indicator) on each. The markup cannot combine underline with the uncontracted flag, so the builder must learn that underlined misspellings are written uncontracted (17.10.3); until then the runner contracts them (sceince -> SCE9CE) and the example stays a mismatch.
